items.q: Why do we struggle to listen when we disagree?
items.a: We believe the myth that **listening means agreeing**.

items.q: What do we do instead of listening?
items.a: We **explain ourselves louder**, which makes the other person **defensive**.

items.q: What did Kasriel's interview with Meles Zenawi teach her?
items.a: Her questions were **masks for confrontation**, so he cut it short and she **learned nothing**.

items.q: What is the first step before listening to someone else?
items.a: **Listen to yourself first**: notice what they trigger, then **set it aside**.

items.q: Which kind of silence does Kasriel recommend?
items.a: **Warm, empathetic silence** that gives them room to **reflect**.
Tuning into what is **important but unspoken**.

items.q: What happened in the BBC/British Council Deep Listening project?
items.a: Over **1,000 people in 100 countries** felt safer, more connected and began **questioning their own attitudes**.

items.q: What happens when people feel truly heard?

items.a: Deeply listen to **someone whose views sting** and notice your **discomfort and resistance**.
